$description: Writing pillar — semantic layer. Generic, tenant-neutral RULE SHAPES: register scale, house-profile deltas, lexicon structure, disclaimer/trademark/contact templates, page-title formula. Composes over writing/primitive.json (craft) and mounts (never copies) project-editorial's register guides for prose exemplars. Ships with lexicon groups EMPTY of tenant values — a per-brand media-assets override (fork-and-repoint, the same pattern themes/<brand>.json uses for color) supplies real terms. DTCG has no array/list primitive; list-shaped rules are modeled as one token per entry, with structural metadata (alternates, exceptions, scope) carried in a documented $extensions.com.pointsav.writing namespace.

table.$description: Wiki-article table color roles — promoted 2026-09-08 from app-mediakit-knowledge's live --k-table-border/-head-bg/-head-ink/-stripe CSS custom properties. Light-mode values only in this pass; dark-mode values are real and live in the engine (--k-table-head-bg: #1b2027, --k-table-stripe: #14181d under html[data-theme="dark"]) but not yet ported here — flagged, not silently dropped. See BRIEF-wiki-infobox-table-tokens.md.

border.$description: Close to but deliberately not aliased to primitive.json's color.neutral-30 (#cdd1d8) — kept as the engine's real live value rather than forcing an inexact match

stripe.$description: Live engine value is a runtime color-mix() (55% head-bg / 45% surface), not a flat literal — this is a static approximation of that computed result at the light-theme surface values, not a byte-exact port

register.$description: Ordered formality/tone scale. Each level's $extensions.guide points at the mounted project-editorial register guide (the composition seam — the SCALE is a token here, the prose exemplar stays project-editorial-owned and mounted, never forked). Mount timing: depends on app-privategit-design's DESIGN-BUNDLE renderer for the editorial bundle — confirm before treating these as live-servable, not just structurally correct.

com.pointsav.writing.note: legacy register-specialist.yaml; RIBA/IFC-derived, no dedicated editorial guide yet

Applies to compliance financial documents in the financial-report-layout / proforma-vehicle-layout family (proformas, commission/rebate breakdowns, tax/governance guides addressed to investors). No dedicated editorial guide yet -- see pattern.financial-disclosure below for the four concrete patterns this register governs.

profile.$description: Per-audience specialization of a register — mirrors project-editorial's house profiles (register + audience delta).

com.pointsav.writing.delta: concept-why-how-code-edge structure; one jargon-free accessibility sentence per section
consequence-first lead; what-it-replaces section; no code

lexicon.$description: Generic banned/required-vocabulary STRUCTURE. Ships EMPTY of tenant values — a brand override (e.g. woodfine-media-assets) supplies real terms, the same fork-and-repoint pattern themes/<brand>.json uses for color aliases. Shape: banned entries carry a preferred-replacement $value; alternates and a define-before-use exception ride in $extensions.

banned.$description: One token per retired/undesired term. $value = preferred replacement. Empty generically — populated only by a tenant override.

required.$description: One token per required-vocabulary term. $value = the canonical phrase; $description = its gloss. Empty generically.

thematic-anchor.$description: Named narrative themes a tenant's voice returns to (e.g. a real tenant's own set of anchor words). Empty generically.

disclaimer.$description: Parametrized disclaimer-protocol TEMPLATE shapes. $value = template string with {slot} placeholders; a tenant override binds the slots to real entity/jurisdiction values. Craft governed by the legal register (writing.semantic.register.legal).

securities-forward-looking.$value: {corporate_entity} operates {technology_subsidiary} as {entity_relationship}. This material contains forward-looking statements under {act_citations}. Material risks include {specific_risks}. {corporate_entity} disclaims any obligation to update except as required by law.

com.pointsav.writing.bcsc_posture: planned/intended/may/target language required for any not-yet-true claim

trademark-footer.$value: {marks} are trademarks of {owner_entity}, used in {jurisdictions}. This notice asserts continuous use in commerce regardless of ™/® omission elsewhere. All other trademarks are the property of their respective owners.

privacy-posture.$value: This interface operates on a {telemetry_scope} architecture.

page-title.$description: Cross-property <title> formula — already ratified as foundry-page-title-formula-v1 in the legacy tree, genuinely generic and already cross-brand (PointSav + Woodfine properties). Per-property display names are the tenant override; the formula itself is not.

separator.$description: em dash, one space each side

pattern.$description: Named, reusable prose moves for a specific document family -- narrower than a register (a posture) or a disclaimer template (a slot-fill string). $value is the shape/rule in one sentence; $extensions carries the triggering circumstance and a real verbatim example pulled from a shipped document, not invented copy.

financial-disclosure.$description: Four recurring prose patterns from the vehicle-proforma document family (financial-report-layout / proforma-vehicle-layout), each illustrated with a representative example using illustrative figures (not sourced from any specific shipped document). Cross-referenced from proforma-vehicle-layout's Governance-note and Basis-of-preparation-checklist sections, which describe WHERE these patterns go; this register describes WHAT to write there.

basis-of-preparation.$value: State issuer type, security issued, holdings/carrying basis, cost-recovery mechanism, tax treatment, and structural caveat, in that order, each clause factual and unhedged; omit an inapplicable clause rather than stating its absence, unless a reader would otherwise wonder whether it applies.

com.pointsav.writing.when: The single closing paragraph of a vehicle proforma (see proforma-vehicle-layout's basis-of-preparation variant for placement).
com.pointsav.writing.example: Basis of preparation. Issuer: a representative single-investor holding corporation. Security: Common Shares, wholly held by the single investor; subscription $1,000,000. ... No carried interest, no arranging party, no offering costs. Cost-recovery: the commission rebate reimburses the issuer's own documented costs ($35,000 ...), capped, no gross-up. The issuer pays an illustrative corporate income tax rate on the taxable (non-sheltered) portion of realized ... distributions -- see the applicable tax guide for the return-of-capital/shelter detail ...
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: State an absence only when a reader would otherwise wonder about it (e.g. an investor comparing vehicle variants) -- not a blanket ban on stating absences, and not a blanket requirement either.

form-note-overlay-opening.$value: One paragraph, three moves in order: what the base document assumes; what triggers the alternate scenario and what specifically changes; what stays the same and who the overlay does not apply to.

com.pointsav.writing.when: The opening paragraph of an optional/alternate-scenario section (see proforma-vehicle-layout's form-note-overlay variant for HTML placement).
com.pointsav.writing.example: The base structure above assumes the issuer bears its own documented costs directly, with no separate arranging party as a payee. Where an arranging party brings the deal and needs reimbursement for its own offering-related costs, the registered dealer instead pays a commission rebate to the issuer only ... a comparable single-investor vehicle has no arranging party -- this overlay applies only to the syndicated form.
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: Never make the reader infer the trigger condition from the restated table alone -- state it in prose.

forward-looking-inline-hedge.$value: Name what's uncertain and the reason, in a clause not a sentence, reusing the document-level BCSC footer's planned/intended/may/target vocabulary rather than inventing new hedge language.

com.pointsav.writing.when: Any figure or paragraph presenting a projection, target, or planned outcome, inline -- distinct from the mandatory document-level footer (a Paper-pillar template), which this pattern does not replace.
com.pointsav.writing.example: ...the unrealized change in stated NAV is not taxed until realized (assumption for tax counsel).
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: A parenthetical, not a paragraph -- the full disclosure lives in the document-level footer; this just flags which specific number is an assumption.

fixed-sum-not-conditioned-on-evidence.$value: State the fixed amount, then explicitly disclaim that it is conditioned on submitting or evidencing any specific cost, whenever 'reimbursement' framing could otherwise imply a documentation requirement that doesn't exist.

com.pointsav.writing.when: A fee or payment is a fixed amount rather than a reimbursement of specific, evidenced costs, and the surrounding language could otherwise be read as implying documentation was required.
com.pointsav.writing.example: ...forwards a fixed offering cost fee of $60,000 to the arranging party -- a reimbursement of offering costs, not a commission. This is a fixed sum; it is not conditioned on the arranging party submitting or evidencing any specific costs incurred.
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: Mandatory, not optional, whenever 'reimbursement' language is used for a fee that is actually a fixed sum -- the reimbursement framing plus no-evidence-required fact together create a real risk of the wrong impression if only one is stated.
